verdicts.reason: Flags are exact at own edge: checkable from interface signals vs. pointer model (full/empty computed from next pointers). Statement is about design structure but with testable exactness; scenario alone is weak. Keep MUST.
Block responsibility table: description of structure, nothing to verify at interface level.
Block responsibility table: description only, nothing to exercise.
Structural wrapper description with no state; nothing to verify.
Write acceptance behaviour stated by quote; checkable by assertion and scenario.
Visibility timing depends on internal retiming flop option and pointers are internal; not checkable every cycle from interface signals. Scenario only.
Empty flag and data change together; observable at interface but the trigger depends on internal write pointer visibility; best exercised by scenario. Actor should be system/slave-side.
Read acceptance and prefetch behaviour stated by quote; data checkable by scoreboard and assertion.
Read pointer visibility to the write side, o_full may fall; scenario appropriate (uses 'may' but the visibility is required).
Occupancy uses internal pointers, not interface signals; checkable via a reference model in a scenario or bound internal assertion, not from interface signals.
Write/read not accepted while full/empty; interface checkable. Strength MUST_NOT is correct.

Occupancy is not an interface signal and views lag across domains, so o_full/o_empty 'whenever' conflicts with conservative lag (empty may be 1 when occupancy >0, which is fine, but full exactness needs a model). Use reference model scenario.
Refers to internal pointer views, not interface signals; needs internal probes or a model.
Pointers and flags change only at own-domain rising clock edge; checkable by assertion.

questions.question: SF-5.4-03 says o_full is 1 whenever occupancy is DEPTH and o_empty is 1 whenever occupancy is 0, but flags are conservative due to cross-domain lag. Is the full/empty guarantee measured with real or visible pointers, and may full/empty also be asserted at occupancy below depth/above zero?
SF-5.3-02 and 5.3-05 depend on whether the retiming flops are present (optional). Which parameter selects them, and should visibility latency checks cover both configurations?
